claims.source_span: Note that the dimension of $B_{\mathbf{n}}$ is $\sum c_{ij} n_i n_j$, where $(c_{ij})$ is the Cartan matrix of $\mathcal{C}$.
claims.claim: dim_k(B_n) = sum_{i,j} c_{ij} n_i n_j where c_{ij} = dim_k Hom(P_i, P_j)
claims.reason: Proved in full in EtingofRepresentationTheory/Chapter9/Discussion_after_Definition9_7_1.lean: `theorem Etingof.finrank_cartanAlgebra (P : ι → C) (n : ι → ℕ) : finrank k ((End (multBiproduct P n))ᵐᵒᵖ) = ∑ i, ∑ j, cartanEntry k P i j * n i * n j`.

claims.source_span: In particular, the algebra $B = B_{\mathbf{n}}$ with the smallest possible dimension, $\sum c_{ij}$, corresponds to the case when all $n_i = 1$
claims.claim: The minimum dimension sum c_{ij} is achieved iff all n_i = 1
claims.reason: Proved in Discussion_after_Definition9_7_1.lean: `theorem Etingof.finrank_cartanAlgebra_eq_sum_cartan_iff` gives the biconditional; the lower bound is `Etingof.sum_cartan_le_finrank_cartanAlgebra` and the base case `Etingof.finrank_cartanAlgebra_one`.

claims.source_span: It is easy to see that this algebra is the only one of the $B_{\mathbf{n}}$ for which $B_{\mathbf{n}}/\operatorname{Rad}(B_{\mathbf{n}}) = \bigoplus_i \operatorname{Mat}_{n_i}(k)$ is commutative.
claims.claim: The semisimple quotient prod_i Mat_{n_i}(k) is commutative iff all n_i = 1
claims.reason: Proved in Discussion_after_Definition9_7_1.lean: `theorem Etingof.semisimpleQuotient_comm_iff {ι : Type*} (n : ι → ℕ) (hn : ∀ i, 1 ≤ n i) : (∀ x y : (∀ i, Matrix (Fin (n i)) (Fin (n i)) k), x * y = y * x) ↔ ∀ i, n i = 1`.

claims.source_span: Thus, we obtain that Morita equivalence classes of finite dimensional algebras are the collections of the form $\{B_{\mathbf{n}}(\mathcal{C}), \mathbf{n} \in \mathbb{N}^m\}$.
claims.claim: The Morita equivalence class of C is exactly {B_n(C) | n in N^m, all n_i >= 1}
claims.reason: Formalized in Introduction_9_7_Morita.lean: `Etingof.nonempty_fgModuleCat_equivalence_of_isBn` (all B_n are Morita equivalent) and `Etingof.ringEquiv_endOp_iff_isBn` (the B_n are exactly all algebras whose module category is C).

claims.claim: Construction of the functor F(M) = Hom(P, M) : C -> B-fmod where B = End(P)^op
claims.reason: The functor is constructed in Theorem9_6_4.lean as `Etingof.IsProgenerator.preadditiveCoyonedaObjFG` (noncomputable def). The blob is setup prose for Theorem 9.6.4, which is fully formalized.

claims.source_span: Note that in such a category, Hom spaces are finite dimensional (check it!).
claims.claim: In a k-linear finite abelian category where every object has finite length and End(X) = k for all simple X, every Hom space is finite dimensional
claims.reason: Fully proved in Introduction_9_6.lean: `theorem Etingof.IsFiniteAbelianCategoryOverField.finiteDimensional_hom (X Y : C) : FiniteDimensional k (X ⟶ Y)` by double induction on filtration length using left-exactness of Hom and Schur's lemma.

claims.source_span: Then all the projective generators of $\mathcal{C}$ are the objects of the form $P_{\mathbf{n}} := \bigoplus_{i=1}^m n_i P_i$, where $n_i \geq 1$ (check it!).
claims.claim: An object Q is a projective generator of C iff Q is isomorphic to bigoplus_i n_i P_i for some n_i >= 1
claims.reason: Fully proved in Introduction_9_7.lean: `theorem Etingof.progenerator_iff_multBiproduct` is an iff; the backward direction `Etingof.isProgenerator_multBiproduct` and forward direction `Etingof.progenerator_decomposition` (using Krull-Schmidt built in KrullSchmidt/) are both complete.

claims.source_span: Defining $B_{\mathbf{n}} = B_{\mathbf{n}}(\mathcal{C}) := \operatorname{End}(P_{\mathbf{n}})^{\mathrm{op}}$, we see that the algebras $B_{\mathbf{n}}$ are all the finite dimensional algebras whose category of finite dimensional modules is equivalent to $\mathcal{C}$.
claims.claim: The algebras B_n = End(P_n)^op are exactly all algebras A with A-fmod equivalent to C
claims.reason: Proved in Introduction_9_7_Morita.lean: `theorem Etingof.ringEquiv_endOp_iff_isBn` gives the biconditional that A is iso to (End Q)^op for some progenerator Q iff A is iso to some B_n.
